course_subtitle: From product manager to Forward Deployed Engineer

weeks.title: Build an agent that can complete a real loop
weeks.goal: By Day 7, the agent completes one useful workflow and exposes every step.

weeks.title: Turn the demo into a system that can recover
weeks.goal: By Day 14, the agent produces predictable outputs and resumes after failure.

weeks.title: Make the system measurable and economically viable
weeks.goal: By Day 21, know how it fails, what it costs, and whether it's improving.

weeks.title: Defend the system like an FDE
weeks.goal: Explain the system to an engineer AND to a non-technical executive. The highest-leverage week for interviews.

days.title: The agent loop
days.one_liner: What an agent actually is, and why most things called agents aren't.

days.title: Tool use
days.one_liner: How a model reaches out and touches a real system.

days.title: Guardrails
days.one_liner: Stopping the agent from doing the wrong thing, including when someone tries to make it.

days.title: Context and memory
days.one_liner: Why stuffing more into the prompt makes the agent worse, not better.

days.title: The audit trail
days.one_liner: If you can't reconstruct the run, you can't fix it or sell it.

days.title: A real workflow
days.one_liner: Pointing all of it at one genuinely manual back-office process.

days.title: Week 1 checkpoint
days.one_liner: Synthesis. Rehearse “walk me through your agent.”

days.title: Structured outputs
days.one_liner: Making the model return something a program can actually use.

days.title: Schema validation
days.one_liner: Checking the shape, and retrying intelligently when it's wrong.

days.title: Failure modes
days.one_liner: The thousand ways it goes wrong. This is the FDE's actual job.

days.title: Checkpointing
days.one_liner: Saving your place so a crash doesn't cost you the whole run.

days.title: Resume
days.one_liner: Picking back up without redoing what already happened.

days.title: Failure handling
days.one_liner: Idempotency: why replaying a step twice must not charge the customer twice.

days.title: Week 2 checkpoint
days.one_liner: Synthesis. Rehearse “what happens when it fails halfway through?”

days.title: Retry logic
days.one_liner: Backoff, jitter, and not making an outage worse by retrying into it.

days.title: Failure categories
days.one_liner: Turning a pile of broken runs into a taxonomy you can act on.

days.title: The golden dataset
days.one_liner: Twenty hand-labelled cases. The highest-leverage thing in this course.

days.title: Running evals
days.one_liner: Scoring it honestly, and why 70% on a hard set beats 100% on an easy one.

days.title: Optimising cost
days.one_liner: Caching, routing, latency budgets, and the cost-per-query number you'll be asked for.

days.title: Multi-agent
days.one_liner: When splitting it up helps, and the live disagreement about whether it ever does.

days.title: Week 3 checkpoint
days.one_liner: Synthesis. Rehearse “how do you know it's working, and what does it cost?”

days.title: The pain point
days.one_liner: Discovery. Finding where time and money actually leak.

days.title: Why AI belongs here
days.one_liner: Rules vs. agent vs. human. Not every step deserves a model.

days.title: Architecture
days.one_liner: Writing down why each component exists — and the enterprise constraints that shaped it.

days.title: Iterations
days.one_liner: Narrating v1 → v2. “Walk me through a complex project you owned.”

days.title: The evals story
days.one_liner: Presenting pass rates, failure categories and open risks to a customer.

days.title: Economics
days.one_liner: The one-page business case, and defending the number in it.

days.title: Rehearsing for an engineer
days.one_liner: Live architecture discussion. Holding technical lines under pressure.

days.title: Rehearsing for a VP
days.one_liner: Answer-first, plain language, bottom-line-up-front. The round most candidates fail.

days.title: Final checkpoint
days.one_liner: The complete case study, and what to do in the 48 hours before an interview.
